# Category model — evaluation report

*Generated by `python -m ml.src.train_category`. Every number below comes from that run; none is written by hand.*

> ## ⚠ These numbers describe a generator, not the real world
>
> This model was trained on **synthetic data**: report text assembled
> from templates, because no labelled corpus of real whistleblowing
> reports exists in this project. Templated text is far easier to
> separate than anything a person writes under stress, so the scores
> below are close to perfect and **say nothing about how this model
> would perform on real reports**.
>
> What they do establish is that the pipeline — validation, leakage
> checks, splitting, vectorising, training, evaluation, artifact
> writing — runs correctly end to end.

## Model-associated keywords

The highest-weighted terms per class. These describe how this model weighs this vocabulary — they are **not** causal explanations, and not reasons a report belongs to a category.

- **CORRUPTION**: `process`, `was`, `any`, `by`, `tender`, `the procurement`, `procurement process`, `procurement`, `without any`, `awarded without`
- **HARASSMENT**: `team`, `one`, `colleague`, `team lead`, `lead`, `keeps`, `senior`, `senior manager`, `people's`, `of`
- **OTHER**: `policy`, `updated`, `merger`, `updated since`, `the merger`, `been updated`, `anyone being`, `consulted`, `being consulted`, `was changed`
- **SECURITY**: `shared`, `left`, `last`, `on shared`, `shared drive`, `left readable`, `was left`, `readable`, `readable on`, `drive`
- **TECHNICAL**: `every`, `queue`, `nightly`, `the nightly`, `nightly export`, `anything`, `dashboard`, `the reporting`, `reporting dashboard`, `for some`

## Priority

Priority is **not** a trained model. No priority or severity labels exist in any dataset here, so a documented, deterministic heuristic is used instead — see `ml/src/priority.py`. It returns the signals that fired alongside the level, and it is advisory: it cannot change a report's category or status.

## Limitations

1. **The training data is synthetic.** This is the limitation that subsumes the rest. Every metric above measures how well the model recovers the rules of a template generator. Real reports are misspelled, elliptical, emotional, written in a second language, and often belong to two categories at once.
2. **The scores are therefore not evidence of usefulness.** They are evidence the pipeline works.
3. **Small vocabulary.** 961 features learned from 573 training documents. Any real report using vocabulary outside it will be classified on very little signal.
4. **Class imbalance persists.** The rarest category has the least training signal, which is exactly where a moderator most needs help.
5. **Confidence is a model probability, not a certainty.** Logistic regression is reasonably calibrated but was not calibration-tested here; a 0.9 does not mean 'right nine times in ten'.
6. **No fairness or bias evaluation.** There is no demographic data to evaluate against — by design, since the system collects none — so differential performance across groups of reporters is unmeasured and unmeasurable here.
7. **English only.**

## Future improvements

1. **Replace the synthetic data with real, moderator-labelled reports.** Nothing else on this list matters until this happens. Phase 7 records moderator overrides, which is the mechanism that accumulates them.
2. Cross-validation once the dataset is large enough to spare the folds.
3. Calibration analysis, so the confidence shown to moderators means what it appears to mean.
4. Per-class thresholds, so a low-confidence suggestion can be withheld rather than shown.
5. Revisit linear TF-IDF only if it demonstrably underperforms on real data — it is fast, explainable and auditable, which are worth a great deal in this setting.
